text:
alex.m: Drafting a short ops cheat-sheet for preemptible GPU evacuations and staggered fallback. Wanted to capture minimal steps + escalation. Thoughts?

maya: Love this. Keep it <5 steps. Add 'stall-kv-cache' note for KV-heavy workloads. :thumbsup:

chris: +1. Also include a short automation snippet to set PodDisruptionBudget override then drain.

alex.m: Rough 5-step: 1) Detect (spot signal > threshold or cloud event) 2) Quarantine affected AZ/pool 3) Drain with staggered windows 4) Reroute traffic to mixed pool / ondemand 5) Post-mortem + cost delta.

jing: For step 3, suggest using stagger windows to avoid thundering herd. e.g., label nodes then drain in batches of N=10. If model loads are large, prefer graceful 5m drain.

alex.m: Example drain command I propose to paste in runbook:

```
# mark node group to evacuate
kubectl label nodes -l pool=preemptible-1 evacuate=true
# drain in batches (example loop)
for node in $(kubectl get nodes -l evacuate=true -o name | head -n 10); do
  kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 || true
  sleep 30
done
```

maya: Add fallback routing policy snippet for model-proxy: route to `model-quantized` first, then `ondemand-gpu` pool -> finally `cpu-fallback` if GPU capacity exhausted.

chris: Autoscaler hooks: set maxUnready to 20% during mass-evac to prevent scale-to-zero oscillations. Also set conservative `scaleDown.delayAfterAdd` during event.

infra-bot: ALERT: detected mass preemptions in us-west-2 (spot-terminate-rate=0.12). Triggered runbook candidate.

oncall: Pinged pager and raised priority. If eviction rate > 10% sustained for 3m, escalate to SRE lead (sre-lead) and infra rotation.

ops-runbooks: Add a single-step rollback for routes so apps can opt out of quantized models under SLA: `route.override=ondemand-gpu`. Also include cost note: short-term spend up to +40% while preserving p99 latency.

alex.m: Ownership: ops-runbooks will own doc + snippets. oncall will own notification thresholds. chris to own autoscaler params. maya to add KV/cache note. jing to test batch drain script in canary.

maya: Small UX note: include a 1-line TL;DR at top for busy oncall: "If spot churn >10% AND request latency impacting p99 -> start staggered evacuation and enable ondemand fallback; escalate after 3m."

chris: +1. Also log a metric `evac.job.duration` and `evac.fallback.count` to help postmortem.

alex.m: I'll push a draft to ops-runbooks repo after lunch. Leaving the thread open for any other edge cases (mixed-arch GPUs, cross-zone traffic).

jing: Edge case: network appliance quotas in some regions mean we can't spin up thousands of ondemand NICs fast. Add region constraint note and prewarm strategy: keep a small warm pool in each critical region.

oncall: Confirmed. Add contact list in runbook: infra-pager, cloud-accounts, cost-ops. Escalation steps: 1) oncall 2) infra rotation 3) SRE lead 4) Eng manager.

alex.m: Great — I'll include all and post back a link once uploaded. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
